title: Lug Cracking on the Forward Engine Mount Side Link — Request for a Life-Limit Removal
abstract: Andes Cargo Lines reports finding indications at the side link lug of the forward engine mount during shop visits and asks for a change that removes the calendar life limit currently attached to the fitting.

sections.request: When our engines come off for a shop visit we are being told to strip and inspect the side link lug on the forward mount, and on three of the last eleven removals the inspector found an indication that had to be dispositioned by Aeralis before we could put the engine back on. Two of those became scrap fittings. The lug carries a life limit that we have to track separately from everything else on the pylon, and because it is not on the same clock as the engine we end up doing pylon work at times that do not suit us. What we want is a fitting that does not need the separate life count and does not surprise us at the last minute during a shop visit. We fly these aircraft on long freight sectors with high thrust settings and we suspect that is part of the story.
sections.background: We took the steel fitting standard when it came out and it did improve things, but the life limit stayed. Across our eleven-aircraft MERIDIAN-46 group we have replaced four fittings in three years, always on the same side. Our engine shop tells us the indications sit at the same radius each time. We have raised this before through the normal reporting route and were told the matter was being watched; we would now like it opened as a change.
sections.expected_outcome: A fitting standard, retrofittable at a normal engine change, that removes the separate life limit and the associated strip inspection at every shop visit, with no increase in the time an engine is off the wing.

type_data.business_justification: Four unplanned fitting replacements in three years, each adding between two and four days to an engine shop visit, against a freight schedule with no spare aircraft.
